skill.name: mobile-native
skill.description: Improve mobile web applications with targeted CSS, viewport metadata, and touch behavior fixes. Use it for safe areas, input zoom, overscroll, hover, gestures, and status bars.
skill.summary: Diagnose and fix browser behaviors that make mobile web applications feel less native.
skill.author: emilkowalski

security_audit.summary: The 79 external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around CSS, HTML, and browser terms. Four reconnaissance findings are also prose-only false positives. Binding a development server to 0.0.0.0 is confirmed because it can expose the server on every network interface.

remediation.suggestion: Recommend loopback by default. For phone testing, warn users to use a trusted network, firewall restrictions, and a temporary development server.

content.user_title: Make Web Apps Feel Native on Mobile
content.value_statement: Mobile web applications often feel awkward because browser defaults conflict with touch interaction and changing viewports. This skill applies focused CSS and metadata fixes for a more native mobile experience.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses common mobile browser issues from supplied application code.
Applies appropriate dynamic or small viewport units for mobile layouts.
Improves touch feedback, hover handling, overscroll, and gesture behavior.
Adds safe-area, viewport, keyboard, and theme metadata guidance.
Distinguishes code-verifiable fixes from behaviors requiring real-device testing.
limitations: Targets mobile web applications, not React Native or other native frameworks.
Cannot confirm physical touch feel, browser chrome behavior, or keyboard behavior without real hardware.
Requires project code and a clear symptom before applying targeted fixes.
Does not replace accessibility, performance, or full cross-browser testing.

use_cases.title: Polish a PWA
use_cases.description: Review viewport, safe-area, status bar, and touch behavior before installation testing.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers building progressive web applications

use_cases.title: Repair Mobile Interactions
use_cases.description: Resolve sticky hover states, slow press feedback, unwanted selection, and gesture conflicts.
use_cases.target_user: Product engineers fixing mobile usability defects

use_cases.title: Audit Responsive Interfaces
use_cases.description: Identify browser-specific issues and separate code fixes from real-device verification tasks.
use_cases.target_user: Design engineers reviewing responsive web interfaces

prompt_templates.title: Check a Mobile Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the supplied mobile web page for sticky hover states, tap highlights, input zoom, and viewport height problems. Apply only relevant fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one page with common mobile browser issues

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Full-Screen Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this full-screen web application. Correct viewport sizing, safe-area padding, overscroll, and bottom controls while preserving accessibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate repair of an application shell or bottom sheet

prompt_templates.title: Improve Touch Gestures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this carousel and drag surface for touch-action conflicts, scroll chaining, selection, and delayed feedback. Explain each applied change.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Mobile Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the supplied PWA across hover, touch, viewport, keyboard, safe-area, theme, and installed-mode behavior. Implement fixes and list hardware checks.

output_examples.input: The bottom action bar disappears behind mobile browser controls.
output_examples.output: The app shell now follows the visible viewport, keeping the action bar above browser controls. Confirm the result on physical iOS and Android devices.

output_examples.input: Carousel swipes move the page vertically and button labels become selected.
output_examples.output: The carousel now reserves horizontal gestures while preserving page scrolling. Selection is disabled only on controls, leaving page content selectable.

output_examples.input: The installed PWA ignores the notch and shows mismatched browser chrome.
output_examples.output: Viewport coverage, safe-area padding, and separate light and dark theme colors were added. Installed-mode behavior still requires device verification.

best_practices: Apply each fix only where its documented browser behavior occurs.
Use capability media queries instead of user-agent or screen-width device detection.
Test touch, keyboard, landscape, and installed modes on physical devices.
anti_patterns: Do not disable page zoom to prevent input focus zoom.
Do not apply selection or gesture restrictions to all page content.
Do not declare mobile behavior fixed using desktop device emulation alone.

faq.question: Does this skill support React Native?
faq.answer: No. It targets mobile browser behavior in web applications and PWAs.

faq.question: Can it verify fixes without a physical phone?
faq.answer: It can verify code changes, but several touch, keyboard, and browser chrome behaviors require real hardware.

faq.question: Will it disable zoom to stop input focus zoom?
faq.answer: No. It preserves accessibility and recommends a minimum input font size instead.

faq.question: Does it handle notches and home indicators?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides viewport coverage and safe-area padding for affected interface elements.

faq.question: Can it improve carousels and drag surfaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It can configure gesture ownership while preserving required page scrolling.

faq.question: Does it replace cross-browser testing?
faq.answer: No. It provides targeted fixes and a verification checklist, but projects still need browser and device testing.
